US Stocks and Crypto Plunge as Democratic Sweep Fuels AI Regulation Fears U.S. stocks and cryptocurrencies plunged amid concerns that Democrats' sweep of both chambers of Congress could lead to tighter regulation of the AI industry. Democrats are also planning to investigate Trump family business dealings, including crypto-related ventures. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.10%, the S&P 500 dropped 3.43%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 2.41% in intraday trading. According to Binance market data, BTC fell 5.97% to $75,695.68, after hitting a low of $75,568, while ETH dropped 7.29% to $2,247.74, with a low of $2,236.78. CoinGlass data shows that $879.92 million in crypto positions were liquidated over the past four hours, including $818.90 million in longs and $61.02 million in shorts. Over the past 24 hours, total liquidations reached $1.03 billion, affecting 198,192 traders, with the largest single liquidation occurring on Binance's ETHUSDT pair at $10.94 million. — link

Core Scientific, Once the Largest Bitcoin Miner, Plans to Fully Shut Down Bitcoin Mining by Q4 2026 Core Scientific, once the world's largest Bitcoin mining company, announced during its Q3 earnings call that it is accelerating the phase-out of its proprietary Bitcoin mining operations. The number of active miners on its network has dropped by nearly 50% compared to the end of 2025, with plans to completely shut down its mining business in Q4 2026 and operate purely as a high-performance computing (HPC) colocation provider starting in 2027. In Q3, the company's colocation revenue reached $215 million (up nearly 60% quarter-over-quarter), and its EBITDA margin expanded to 57%. — link

Largest HYPE Treasury Firm Hyperliquid Strategies Seeks US Futures Commission Merchant Registration, Reports $620.6M Quarterly Profit Hyperliquid Strategies (NASDAQ: PURR), the largest publicly traded HYPE treasury company, announced that a subsidiary has applied for registration as a US futures commission merchant (FCM). If approved, the entity plans to serve US clients trading perpetual futures on permissioned markets under Hyperliquid's proposed HIP-3* framework. The company also reported $620.6 million in net income for the quarter ended September 30, primarily driven by $803 million in unrealized gains on its HYPE holdings. It raised $911 million in equity capital during the quarter, spending $785 million to acquire approximately 9.1 million HYPE tokens. As of October 28, its total holdings had reached approximately 38.9 million HYPE, with an average cost of $56.35 per token. — link
